<STRUCT_0001>
Before we characterize locally quasi-finite morphisms in terms of coverings
we do it for quasi-DM morphisms.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic stacks.
The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is quasi-DM,
<STRUCT_0003> for any morphism <MATH_0003> with <MATH_0004> an algebraic space
there exists a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented, locally
quasi-finite morphism <MATH_0005> where
<MATH_0006> is an algebraic space, and
<STRUCT_0004> there exist algebraic spaces <MATH_0007>, <MATH_0008> and a morphism
<MATH_0009> which is surjective, flat, and
locally of finite presentation, and a morphism
<MATH_0010> which is surjective, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and locally quasi-finite.
<STRUCT_0005>

The implication (2) <MATH_0001> (3) is immediate.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume (1) and let <MATH_0002> be as in (2). Then
<MATH_0003> is quasi-DM, see
Lemma <REF_0001>.
By
Lemma <REF_0002>
the algebraic space <MATH_0004> is DM, hence quasi-DM. Thus
<MATH_0005> is quasi-DM by
Lemma <REF_0003>.
Hence we may apply
Theorem <REF_0004>
to get the morphism <MATH_0006>
as in (2).

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Assume (3). Let <MATH_0007> and
<MATH_0008> be as in (3).
To prove that <MATH_0009> is quasi-DM it suffices to show that
<MATH_0010> is quasi-DM, see
Lemma <REF_0005>.
By
Lemma <REF_0006>
we see that <MATH_0011> is quasi-DM.
Hence <MATH_0012> is quasi-DM by
Lemma <REF_0007>
and (1) holds. This finishes the proof of the lemma.
